4.1.intro: Your brand core is one page about who you are. Everything you write comes from it.

steps.say: Describe 2 or 3 types of customer. For each: what they want, what bugs them, and where they hang out online.
steps.check: You have 2 or 3 short customer notes.
steps.lost: Describe one customer in three lines.

steps.say: Write one sentence: why should people choose you?
steps.check: You have one promise sentence.
steps.lost: Finish this: "Choose us because ..."

steps.say: Pick three words for how you sound. Pick three words you never use.
steps.check: You have a six-word voice guide.
steps.lost: Three words you are. Three words you're not.

steps.say: Write two or three values. Next to each, write one thing you really do that proves it.
steps.check: Every value has proof.
steps.lost: One value, and one thing you do that shows it.

steps.say: Write your story in under 100 words: why your brand exists. Save all five answers on one page.
steps.check: One brand page is saved where helpers and tools can read it.
steps.lost: Write why you started, in a few lines. Save the page.

4.2.intro: A customer profile describes one type of buyer, using their real words. Real words beat guesses.

steps.say: Collect 30 to 50 real customer quotes from reviews, a short survey and support emails.
steps.check: You have one document of real quotes.
steps.lost: Copy 10 customer quotes into one document.

steps.say: For one profile, write their age range and life stage. Then write the job your product does for them.
steps.check: The profile has a who and a why.
steps.lost: Who are they? What problem do you solve for them?

steps.say: Add their top 3 worries and the exact words they use for the problem and the product.
steps.check: You have phrases you can copy into ads.
steps.lost: Write three worries in their words.

steps.say: Add where they shop and what they compare you with. Then do the same for each profile.
steps.check: You know your real competitors and channels.
steps.lost: Write where they shop. One place is enough for now.

4.3.intro: Brand guidelines are a short guide anyone can follow, so everything looks like you.

steps.say: Add your logo versions and how much empty space to leave around them.
steps.check: Each logo has a clear-space rule.
steps.lost: Put your logo on a page. Note: leave space around it.

steps.say: Add your colours with their hex codes (like #0B1F3A), and your fonts and sizes.
steps.check: Anyone can match your colours and fonts.
steps.lost: Write your main colour code and your font name.

steps.say: Describe your photo and video style: light, framing and props. Add 3 example images.
steps.check: A freelancer could shoot on-brand from this page.
steps.lost: Add three photos you love the look of.

steps.say: Add good and bad examples of your voice, and do's and don'ts for ads, emails and posts. Share it as one link or PDF.
steps.check: The guide is done and shared.
steps.lost: Add one good and one bad example. Share the link.

4.4.intro: Content pillars are the 4 to 6 topics you always post about. They stop the blank-page feeling.

steps.say: Write your 4 to 6 topics. Ideas: proof, teaching, story and community, product and offer.
steps.check: You have a list of topics.
steps.lost: Pick four topics from the ideas list.

steps.say: For each place you post, decide how much of each topic to use. Use the lesson table to start.
steps.check: Each channel's mix adds up to 100%.
steps.lost: Copy the lesson table's mix for now.

steps.say: Plan one month of posts using that mix.
steps.check: You have a month of ideas, each with a topic and a channel.
steps.lost: Plan one week of posts first.

steps.say: Write what goes in each topic. **Proof:** reviews, customer photos, press. **Teaching:** how to use, myths, care. **Story and community:** you, behind the scenes, customers. **Product and offer:** launches, restocks, bundles, sales.
steps.check: Every topic has a short list of post types.
steps.lost: Write two post ideas under each topic.

steps.say: Check your month against a rough mix: 40% teaching and proof, 30% story and community, 30% product and offer.
steps.check: Your plan follows the mix.
steps.lost: Count your posts by topic. Roughly right is fine.

steps.say: Fill gaps with ideas that never run out: reviews, comments, support questions ("You asked, we answered"), and a regular series.
steps.check: You have more ideas than posting slots.
steps.lost: Turn one customer question into a post.

4.5.intro: A calendar shows what you'll post and when. Plan around your sales dates.

steps.say: Mark your big dates first: launches, sales, Mother's Day, Black Friday.
steps.check: Your key dates are on the calendar.
steps.lost: Write your next three big dates.

steps.say: Add product stories and tips in the 2 weeks around each date.
steps.check: Each sale has warm-up posts.
steps.lost: Add two posts before your next sale.

steps.say: Fill the gaps with community posts and happy-customer posts.
steps.check: Every week has at least 3 posts planned.
steps.lost: Add one customer post each week.

steps.say: Before reposting a customer's photo or video, message them and get a written yes.
steps.check: You have a saved yes for every customer post.
steps.lost: Always ask first. Save their yes.

4.6.intro: Free posts are a free way to test ad ideas. Posts people watch usually make good ads.

steps.say: Film 3 to 5 short videos in one or two sessions a week. Post them across the week.
steps.check: You post 3 to 5 videos a week without filming every day.
steps.lost: Film three short videos in one go.

steps.say: After 48 hours, check each post's watch time in the app's insights.
steps.check: You know which 1 or 2 posts held attention best.
steps.lost: Which video did people watch longest?

steps.say: Where the app has a test post feature, like Instagram trial reels, use it. It shows a post to people who don't follow you first.
steps.check: You can try ideas on new people safely.
steps.lost: Optional. Skip if your app doesn't have it.

steps.say: Reply to every comment in the first hour after posting.
steps.check: Comments get quick answers.
steps.lost: Reply to comments soon after you post.

steps.say: Add your best post to your ad ideas list.
steps.check: Your next ad starts from an idea that worked.
steps.lost: Write your best post's name on your ad list.

4.7.intro: A community is customers who talk to you and each other. It works best when people buy again.

steps.say: Check how often customers buy again. In Shopify: **Analytics > Reports > New vs returning customers**. If people rarely rebuy, focus on reviews and creators instead and skip this lesson.
steps.check: You know if community is worth it for you.
steps.lost: Do people buy again? If rarely, skip this lesson. That's okay.

steps.say: Give customers a place and a reason to talk: a private group, events, challenges, or sharing their photos.
steps.check: You have one community space with a clear reason to join.
steps.lost: Pick one place for customers to chat.

steps.say: Make customers the star of your posts, not the product.
steps.check: At least one post a week stars a customer.
steps.lost: Share one customer photo this week (with their yes).

steps.say: Read their questions each week. Add new ones to your worries list from Lesson 3.3.
steps.check: Your ideas and FAQ grow from real questions.
steps.lost: Write down one new question each week.

steps.say: Run a poll so customers help choose something: a colour, a name or a flavour.
steps.check: Customers had a say.
steps.lost: Post one poll.

steps.say: Use real customers as the faces of a collection.
steps.check: Real customers appear in your marketing.
steps.lost: Ask one customer to be in a photo.

steps.say: Run a small event or live session. Reward your biggest fans with early access, gifts or a VIP group.
steps.check: Your keenest fans feel looked after.
steps.lost: Send one thank-you gift to a big fan.

steps.say: Share feedback you acted on. For example: "You asked for bigger sizes. Here they are."
steps.check: Customers see their voice matters.
steps.lost: Post one "you asked, we did it" update.

4.8.intro: When people see the person behind the brand, they trust it more. Press mentions add proof.

steps.say: Post one founder post a week: an opinion, behind the scenes, or a lesson you learned.
steps.check: People see a real person every week.
steps.lost: Post one behind-the-scenes photo this week.

steps.say: Each month, pitch one story (not a product) to a journalist or podcast. For example, your journey or a trend.
steps.check: You sent a pitch and wrote it down.
steps.lost: Send one short pitch email this month.

steps.say: When you get press, add their logo and a quote to your home page and ads.
steps.check: Press proof shows where shoppers decide.
steps.lost: Got press? Add the logo to your home page.

4.9.intro: Creators can spread your brand fast. Send widely, then pay to run the best posts as ads.

steps.say: Send free product to 20 or more creators who match your customer.
steps.check: Product is on its way to lots of creators.
steps.lost: Send product to five creators to start.

steps.say: Pay the best ones for usage rights (permission to use their video in your ads) for a set time, like 3 months.
steps.check: You have signed permission to run their content as ads.
steps.lost: Ask your best creator for permission to use their video in ads. Get it in writing.

steps.say: Run their content as partnership ads. These show the creator's name in the ad header, usually next to your brand. See Modules 5, 7 and 19.
steps.check: The ads are live and you can compare them with your own ads.
steps.lost: Turn one creator video into an ad.
